title: WebCTRL Setpoint Blocked by Instructor Priority 3
description: Runs the AHU static-pressure loop, forces its setpoint low at instructor Priority 3, and later releases that slot so students can prove why a valid WebCTRL write at a lower BACnet priority does not become effective.

events.description: Pin the effective setpoint at Priority 3
Relinquish Priority 3 so WebCTRL or the default becomes effective
Keep the timeline open for recovery evidence

expected_results: During the Priority-3 force, WebCTRL can acknowledge a lower-priority write while present value remains 0.25 in. H2O
Fan speed and measured static respond to the effective value rather than the student's requested value
After Priority 3 is released, the WebCTRL command or relinquish default immediately regains authority while physical pressure recovers with PID/fan lag
completion_criteria: Student inspects the priority array before blaming the controller or network
Student releases their own test command and verifies the expected effective value and process recovery
instructor_notes: A real WebCTRL Priority-16 command makes the recovery more obvious; without one, the point returns to its 1.0 in. H2O relinquish default. Preflight priority reconciliation remains separate from this deliberate scenario-owned Priority-3 event.
student_objectives: Distinguish accepted write from effective present value
Use BACnet priority arrays and relinquish correctly
